gaps.sentence: Luckily I ___ find a parking space right outside the theatre.
gaps.hint: one particular success on that occasion
gaps.explanation: One particular success takes 'was able to': was able to find.

gaps.sentence: I ___ work late every Wednesday this month; it is a new company policy.
gaps.hint: obligation imposed by an external rule
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' expresses obligation imposed by external rules: have to work.

gaps.sentence: I have no idea where he is — he ___ have gone to the gym, or maybe to the pool.
gaps.hint: an uncertain guess about the past
gaps.explanation: 'Might have' expresses an uncertain guess about the past: might have gone.

gaps.sentence: I ___ to wear a uniform at my last job, and I hated it.
gaps.hint: an obligation imposed in the past
gaps.explanation: Past obligation is expressed with 'had to': had to wear.

gaps.sentence: You ___ better take some cash — the stall does not take cards.
gaps.explanation: 'Had better' warns about a sensible action: had better take.

gaps.sentence: Library books ___ be taken out of the reading room.
gaps.hint: a passive prohibition with mustn't be
gaps.explanation: Prohibitions can be passive: mustn't be taken.

gaps.sentence: Do I ___ to bring my own towel, or is one provided?
gaps.hint: a question about necessity with do
gaps.explanation: Questions about necessity use 'do ... have to': have to bring.

gaps.sentence: I ___ have known you were in hospital — nobody told me.
gaps.explanation: 'Couldn't have' means it was impossible to do: couldn't have known.
